transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Rajan (Snowcap CTO), Lisa (Head of Search), Connor (Infra)

Summary:
Quick qualify/discovery to map Snowcap's embedding rerank needs; focused on throughput, dims, fanout economics, and private hosting constraints. Agreed to run a smoke test and exchange security docs.

Topics: Fanout/sharding tradeoffs, embedding dimensionality, hybrid recall->rerank pipeline, caching (KV/prefix), SLAs and fallback to hosted variants.

Action items (captured verbally during call): see metadata list.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this - Diego from our SE team will jump in on the technical bits. Quick intros?
[00:12] Rajan (Snowcap): Rajan here, CTO. We're trying to replace parts of our search stack with embeddings + rerank, current infra is Elastic + some homegrown rerank. Concerned about throughput.
[00:20] Lisa (Snowcap): Lisa - I run search. Our goal is under 200ms P95 on product queries and 50ms on cache hits but we get big spikes during promotions.
[00:28] Diego (Redwood): Got it. Can you describe current qps and fanout? rough numbers are ok.
[00:32] Connor (Snowcap): Baseline is 120 qps steady, peaks to ~2k during promos. Typical fanout today is 200 candidates pre-rerank, embedding dim 1536 for accuracy.
[00:44] Diego (Redwood): 200 fanout with 1536 dims is heavy. Two levers we usually look at: reduce dim (768 or compact embeddings) and then run a lightweight recall + rerank where rerank uses a smaller model or quantized variant.
[00:56] Rajan: We're sensitive to quality regressions though; can't afford worse relevance on PLG features.
[01:04] Maya: totally. That's why teams often pilot hybrid: hosted for baseline (fast rollouts) and Dedicated reserved capacity for peak or private traffic. That gives cheaper steady state but a guaranteed throughput path for spikes.
[01:18] Lisa: Question on security: we need SOC2 type 2, SAML SSO, and KMS integration for encryption. Do you support HSM/KMS and audit logs?
[01:28] Diego: Yes, on Private and Dedicated we can integrate customer KMS, HSM via the standard connectors; we emit audit logs and SSO via SAML/Okta; hosted has a SOC2 report we can share. I'll follow up with the docs.
[01:40] Rajan: Also curious about data residency; some of our EU traffic needs to stay in eu-west-1.
[01:46] Maya: we have region pinning and private control plane options, we'll include region info in the security pack.
[01:52] Connor: How does the fanout interact with vector DBs? We run Milvus currently and are evaluating Pinecone for managed. If we fanout 200 to vdb every query that's a lot of network I/O.
[02:06] Diego: two common approaches: 1) shard the index so fanout goes to fewer nodes (but costs more to manage), 2) do hybrid recall where you do a coarse low-dim recall first (e.g., 768 or sparse) to get 100, then rerank locally; or 3) use caching at prefix/KV level to avoid repeated retrievals for similar queries.
[02:24] Lisa: What's the impact on tail latency if we add a KV cache in front of the vdb?
[02:28] Diego: if it's a well-warmed prefix cache, tail latency can drop significantly - we typically see P99 reductions, but cache hit patterns matter. Also, KV cache plus continuous batching in our runtime helps reduce per-token cost.
[02:42] Rajan: Pricing: we need a back-of-envelope for hosted per-1M queries vs dedicated monthly commit.
[02:48] Maya: we'll send a pricing matrix; to ballpark, hosted cost scales linearly with tokens/embeds; Dedicated is better for predictable high throughput nights - Diego can give rough numbers after we know embedding dims and QPS.
[03:00] (pause)
[03:10] Connor: What about quantization for embeddings? We saw a paper about 8-bit sparse embedding quantization. Is that something Redwood supports at serving?
[03:20] Diego: Yes, quantization is supported in the runtime for model variants — but there's a tradeoff in recall. For embeddings we more commonly compress offline (productizing smaller dims) or use hybrid dense+sparse. We can run evals to quantify quality drop at 8-bit vs float16.
[03:38] Lisa: So for a pilot, we'd want to see a) throughput numbers for our index size, b) quality comparison: 1536->768->quantized, c) hosting options cost.
[03:50] Maya: that's a great checklist. Our typical pilot is a 2-4 week scoped PoC: smoke throughput test, small relevance set for eval, and then a production pilot with guarded rollouts.
[04:04] Rajan: timeline: procurement in 4-6 weeks ideally. We want to decide on hosting by end of quarter.
[04:12] Maya: sounds doable. Diego, want to walk through a potential smoke test config?
[04:16] Diego: sure. For the smoke test we'll need a sample of the index (document vectors or the originals), QPS traces for a 1-hour window, and target SLAs. We'll provision a Dedicated worker pool sized to simulate 2k peak with autoscale off so we can measure tail latency.
[04:34] Connor: we can share a 10% slice of the index and a synthetic trace. We'll need guidance on obfuscation for PII.
[04:40] Maya: we routinely accept obfuscated datasets; we'll provide a checklist.
[04:44] Rajan: What about fallback? If Dedicated saturates do you fallback to hosted? Latency spikes are unacceptable so I'd prefer prioritized routing rather than full failure.
[04:54] Diego: yes, routing policies allow fallback to a hosted-compatible model or to a lower-dim variant; you can define cost vs latency priorities. We also support canary and automatic fallback policies. There's no hard outage — it's graceful degradation to a cheaper or lower-latency path.
[05:08] Lisa: Any notes about KV cache invalidation? Our inventory churns during promos.
[05:12] Diego: TTL-based invalidation plus workload-aware batching. For high-churn keys we recommend shorter TTLs and rely on batching to keep throughput efficient.
[05:22] Maya: A quick real example: a retail customer saw 3x cheaper per-query cost by moving cold recall to hosted low-dim embeddings and keeping the rerank on a Dedicated pool during peak.
[05:34] Rajan: Competitors — Pinecone and Weaviate — what do you see as main deltas?
[05:38] Maya: Pinecone focuses on vector DB as core; our delta is unified inference runtime + routing and built-in rerank with kernel selection for LLMs. Weaviate has modules but less of a production serving focus for LLM throughput. We'll send a short competitor note.
[05:54] Connor: For the smoke test, do you need access to our VPC or can we run against hosted endpoints?
[05:58] Diego: both options; easiest to start against hosted endpoints for quick results, then move to Private/VPC for exact latencies. If you need a private control plane we can emulate in a customer-managed VPC.
[06:10] Lisa: Any special auth for VPC? We use SAML + mTLS in our internal clusters.
[06:15] Diego: we support mTLS and SAML for the control plane; cables and cert rotation are standard. We'll include config examples.
[06:24] Maya: ok let's capture next steps: we'll run a short smoke test, share security pack, and get pricing.
[06:30] Rajan: sounds good. Connor will share the sample index and traces by Monday.
[06:36] Connor: yep, I'll aim for 2026-06-21.
[06:40] Diego: I'll draft the smoke test infra and sizing; planning to provision a Dedicated pool to simulate 2k peak and a hosted fallback.
[06:50] Maya: I'll send pricing and the SOC2/KMS docs by Tues.
[06:54] (pause)
[07:02] Lisa: One more question — how do you measure model-level regressions for rerank? We need regression alerts for NDCG drop.
[07:10] Diego: we integrate with eval sets and can run A/B or canary evaluations. Redwood Optimize can monitor quality metrics and trigger rollback or alerts if metrics degrade beyond thresholds. We'll include a sample eval harness.
[07:26] Rajan: Great. Also, curious about billing: does Dedicated have overage billing or hard cap?
[07:32] Maya: Dedicated is committed capacity; there are burst options and pre-agreed overage rates. We'll include the matrix.
[07:40] Connor: On the infra side, we need to confirm whether the KV cache is colocated with dedicated nodes or if it can be external (redis) — both are possible?
[07:48] Diego: both are possible; colocation reduces network hops and often improves tail latency. External Redis is fine for flexibility. We'll provide recommendations.
[07:58] (several quick clarifications, overlap)
[08:12] Maya: that's most of our questions. Any blockers for the pilot?
[08:16] Rajan: procurement lead time is the only blocker; otherwise technical looks ok. Security will want the SOC2 and network diagram.
[08:24] Maya: we'll get that over.
[08:28] Diego: I'll also include a suggested embedding sweep: 1536 -> 1024 -> 768 -> 512 and quantized eval points; that usually helps map accuracy vs econ.
[08:44] Lisa: ok that helps.
[08:46] (closing remarks)
[08:50] Maya: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and Diego will coordinate the smoke test.
[08:56] Rajan: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:00] Call ended.

Notes about transcription: minor ASR errors on technical acronyms ("kay vee cache" sometimes), some speaker overlaps near the end.
